Overview

What each stage covers

StageStatusEvidenceProvesDoes not prove
Bugs

Every catalogued fix

One row per fix the rule-based catalog admitted. Days, commits and releases come from Method A: the time since the commit that last touched the lines the fix changed. Select a row for its evidence.

Timeline

Lifespans across the history

Each bar runs from the nominated introducing commit to the fix. Drag the scrubber to see which bugs were alive on a given day.

Commit × test results

Each square is one commit run in Docker without network. Feasibility rows build the crate and run its unit tests; sweep rows run one bug's regression test.

Patterns

What the history keeps doing

Each card counts rows in the bundle and names the test in this repository that locks the rule behind it. Cards without a locking test say so.

Method

Method A against Method B

A · blame (SZZ)

For each fix, blame the lines it removed or changed. The latest commit that touched them is the nominated introducer. Cheap and covers every fix, but it names who last edited the line, not who broke it.

B · behavioural sweep

Write a regression test for the bug, then run it at earlier commits in Docker. The first failing commit is where the behaviour broke. Exact when located; a lower bound when old commits do not build.

Ask the repo

Search the evidence

Ranked search over fix subjects, SHAs and patterns. Results are rows from the bundle, never generated text.

Ask Claude about these results

Sends only the rows above (and the headline metrics) to Claude on your own account. The answer is shown only if every cited SHA exists in those rows and every number in it appears in them.

Citation checker

The same check runs on every answer from Claude. Run it on a made-up answer that cites a SHA and a number the data does not contain.

Reproduce

Rebuild every number yourself

The bundle is produced by scripts; nothing in it was written by hand or by a model. These commands rebuild it from the target repository at its pinned commit.
